justifications.problem-significance: Identifying, formalizing, and empirically testing candidate laws of biology across diverse taxa and scales is a genuinely difficult, open-ended, and scientifically consequential problem (`repo/README.md`, `captured/mcp-overview.json`). The snapshot demonstrates why this separation of mathematical proof from biological reality matters: across 1,702 extracted claims (including 162 with formal mathematical statements and 63 established theorems), only 2 mathematical claims are currently supported by data measured on living organisms (`captured/mcp-overview.json`, `captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`). Grounding historical and modern theoretical claims (Darwin, Thompson, Wolfram, Levin, Aristotle, and mathematical biology) against 1,036 resolved taxa and 1,372 provenanced datasets (`repo/test-data/organisms/README.md`, `captured/mcp-organisms.json`) addresses a real epistemic bottleneck in theoretical and comparative biology, though much of the current corpus still consists of historical book claims rather than modern open frontier hypotheses.
justifications.scientific-impact: The project achieved substantial, concrete outputs in ~23 hours (`captured/git-stats.txt`): 1,702 claims extracted with verbatim quotes, 880 nanopublications live on the production registry (`repo/README.md`, `captured/nanopub-manifests.txt` showing 2,085 production lines across Darwin, Thompson, and Wolfram manifests), 47 Lean 4 formalizations compiled without `sorry` (`captured/lean-reports.txt`), and 133 claims tested against data (66 on biological organisms, yielding 78 supports, 25 mixed, 21 refutes, and 9 inconclusive in `repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`). Technical rigor is particularly evident in the negative segmenter-bias control (`captured/forum-feed.json` post `69f0d5d4-544e-49c4-8156-a409791f233c`, showing Cellpose-SAM rounds brick-wall controls toward 120 degrees and lowering `thompson1917-ch07-04` confidence from 0.6 to 0.35), the Fittest MLIP equivariance and stretched-bond calibration audit (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`), and the discovery of upstream nanopub v2.0 template namespace and `nanopub-java` exit-code bugs (issue #37 in `captured/github-issues.json`). It falls short of a higher score because 59 of the 133 tests are computational cellular-automaton/Turing-machine enumerations from Wolfram (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`), test verdicts are not yet wired into `status` in `docs/claims.json` (issue #39), and the A9 faithfulness assessor has run on 0 of the data tests (issue #40).
justifications.decentralized-agency: While the project uses multiple model providers (Claude as builder; GPT, Gemini, and Grok as blind assessors in `captured/subagent-sessions.txt` and `repo/BEST_PRACTICES.md`) and parallel cloud-agent branches (`captured/git-log.txt`, `captured/github-prs.json` PRs #18-#33), the workflow is centrally orchestrated by a human lead (`repo/chats/README.md` shows 22 human-driven sessions directing every task and merge; issue #61 candidly notes that 'decentralization is mostly different providers assess blind and the forum, with a human in the loop for publishing'). The Science Claw forum (`https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev`) and MCP tools provide infrastructure for decentralized coordination, but `captured/forum-feed.json` and `captured/forum-requests.json` show all 12 posts and 4 open requests were authored by `delphisci` with 0 comments and 0 external offers, and the 3-post `thompson1917-ch07-04` arc was scripted via `node forum/client.mjs batch forum/posts/thompson-ch07-04-arc.json` (`repo/forum/README.md`). Thus, agents execute well-scoped parallel batches and blind audits, but do not autonomously pick up, hand off, and revise work without central human planning.
justifications.collective-capability: The evidence pack contains no controlled experimental comparison in the repository measuring multi-agent vs. single-agent, collaborative vs. isolated, or decentralized vs. centralized performance on the same task (explicitly confirmed by the builders in issue #61: 'today I believe we don't have one and that is the 25% criterion'; while issue #41 mentions a 'four-arm agent comparison harness' with two 20-claim experiments, no files, paths, or data from that harness exist in `captured/tree.txt`). The only quantitative multi-model analysis present in the pack is the post-hoc leave-one-out routing ledger over 99 decisive data tests in `repo/plugins/fittest/README.md` (issue #57), where filtering GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.7 truth scores by inter-model agreement and confidence raises accuracy on trusted claims from 0.83 (99 claims, 17 silent errors) to 0.935 (77 trusted claims, 22 flagged, catching 12 of 17 errors). Because that compares a 2-model disagreement filter against the unfiltered 2-model mean rather than collective vs. single-agent task execution, the core comparison requested by the rubric is missing.
justifications.execution-validation: This is a real, deployed, externally usable system with multiple independent validation layers rather than a concept or slide deck. The MCP server is live at `https://delphisci-mcp.fly.dev/mcp` (10 Fly releases, 1,522 tool calls and 60 sessions logged in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) and was validated by an independent 100-case test suite checking responses against direct TriG parses (93/100 pass, 100% agreement between hosted and local `origin/main`, median latency 32 ms in issue #56). Nanopublications are live and queryable on the Knowledge Pixels network (`captured/nanopub-manifests.txt`, `captured/mcp-morpholib-live.json` verifying 109 production MorphoEval nanopubs). However, the executable-claim runner (`repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`) was only run on 6 data claims in the captured snapshot, with 3 `reproduced` and 3 `drifted` (`darwin1859-ch10-12`, `darwin1859-ch10-16`, `darwin1859-ch12-11` drifting on byte sizes and Spearman rho `-0.2258` vs `-0.2189`), and 4 Thompson tests require manual browser downloads bypassed in `repo/scripts/exec/overrides.json`.
justifications.collaboration-bonus: The team published live, zero-auth infrastructure (`https://delphisci-mcp.fly.dev/mcp`, `npx -y github:fractastical/delphi`, and `https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev`), documented active outreach in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md` (offering math-bio and collagen rigidity scaling anchors to `InquilineKea` and SentiLab in `scienceclaw-e14-hackathon-room-ws`, sharing the MCP server on Discord with `Symplectic Geometry of Awe` and `Joshua G`), and ran an empirical pilot of another participant's tool (`Fittest MCP` by Pavel-Tk, `repo/plugins/fittest/README.md` and issue #57) that identified a concrete calibration flaw in sparse buckets (a 2x stretched C-O bond in alanine trusted at 0.67 on 3 DFT labels) and adapted Fittest's Beta-posterior routing to delphisci truth scores. However, as issue #41 explicitly states ('We have things worth reusing and zero observed reuse, which scores zero. An offer is not evidence') and `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md` confirms (unidentified MCP client bursts like `corpus-census` and `frontier-adapters` cannot be tied to external teams, and Fittest's author is marked 'Not contacted yet'), there is no documented uptake Enabling another team's result, placing this squarely at anchor 5.

problem-significance: Expand empirical testing on the modern biological frontier (`claim-sources/levin-papers/`, where only 2 of 310 claims are tested in `captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`, and `claim-sources/math-bio-claims/`, where 0 of 21 are data-tested) so the problem demonstrated is not predominantly historical 19th/20th-century claims.
Ground claim entities to external biological identifiers (HGNC, GO, NCBITaxon) as proposed in issue #34 so cross-graph mechanistic tests become systematic rather than ad-hoc.
scientific-impact: Wire `test-data/claim-tests/*/*/result.json` verdicts directly into the claim `status` field in `docs/claims.json` and publish the 133 claim-test evidence nanopubs to production (issue #39, `captured/nanopub-manifests.txt`).

Run the independent A9 faithfulness assessor across the biological data tests (currently 0 of 16+ in issue #40) to verify that each test script operationalizes the exact biological claim rather than a convenient proxy.

Execute the 8 pending pre-registered Levin/Thompson tests (`captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`, e.g., `levin-2018-hcn2-06`, `thompson1917-ch08-01`, `thompson1917-ch08-02`) to raise the count of math claims supported in organisms above 2.
decentralized-agency: Run a live multi-agent loop on the Science Claw forum (`https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev`) where independent agents autonomously claim open requests (`captured/forum-requests.json`), execute tests or reviews, and post results via `delphi_log_test_result` without human batch scripting (`forum/posts/thompson-ch07-04-arc.json`).

Automate the trigger from Fittest's `exec_queue` (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`) to claim-test execution and blind A9 faithfulness review so agents hand off work through shared repository/forum state rather than waiting for human chat prompts (`repo/chats/README.md`).
collective-capability: Commit and run a clean, pre-registered benchmark on a fixed sample of claims (e.g., 20-30 claims from the 99 decisive data tests) comparing single-agent, isolated multi-agent, and collective builder+blind-assessor+remediation workflows on error detection, dataset URL validity, and accuracy against ground-truth verdicts (closing the gap noted in issue #61 and committing the four-arm harness mentioned in issue #41).

Extend `repo/plugins/fittest/README.md` (`route.py`) to report each individual model's standalone accuracy (GPT-5.6 Sol alone vs. Grok 4.7 alone) alongside the routed committee accuracy (0.935) and remediation lift.
execution-validation: Fix the 3 drifting data tests in `repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json` (`darwin1859-ch10-12`, `darwin1859-ch10-16`, `darwin1859-ch12-11`) by excluding non-deterministic fetch metadata from `derived/files.json` comparisons and pinning RNG seeds/API snapshots, then run `npm run claims:exec` across all 47 Lean proofs and 133 data tests.
Apply the one-line Windows path fix in `mcp/lib.mjs` and the input-validation/SPARQL fixes from Amit's MCP test report (issue #56, PR #36) so all 100/100 MCP test cases pass.
collaboration-bonus: Send the Fittest pilot findings and sparse-bucket calibration bug report (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`, issue #57) to Pavel-Tk and log their acknowledgement or code/calibration update in `COLLABORATIONS.md`.

Get at least one external team (`InquilineKea`, `Symplectic Geometry of Awe`, or `Joshua G` from `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) to log a query, claim proposal, or test result on `https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev` or link a commit/issue in their repo showing reuse of `delphisci-mcp`.

comparison_found.note: No multi-agent vs. single-agent or decentralized vs. centralized task execution comparison exists in the pack (confirmed by issue #61; issue #41 mentions a 'four-arm agent comparison harness' on 20 claims, but no files or results from it exist in captured/tree.txt). The closest measurement is in repo/plugins/fittest/README.md (and issue #57), which evaluates leave-one-out disagreement routing across two assessors (GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.7) on 99 decisive data tests: trusting all mean scores yields 0.83 accuracy (17 silent failures), whereas escalating high-disagreement/low-confidence claims yields 0.935 accuracy on the 77 trusted claims and catches 12 of 17 errors.

top_three_fixes: Run and commit a direct single-agent vs. multi-agent/collective ablation benchmark (or commit the four-arm comparison harness data referenced in issue #41 and extend `plugins/fittest/route.py` with single-model baselines) on a subset of the 133 tested claims (raises `collective-capability`, 25% weight, from 3 to 7+).

Demonstrate autonomous agent-to-agent handoff on the live Science Claw forum (`https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev`) by having non-builder agents pick up open requests (`captured/forum-requests.json`), run A9 faithfulness audits (issue #40) or pending Levin tests (`captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`), and post results via MCP without human batch scripts (raises `decentralized-agency`, 20% weight, from 4 to 7).

Fix the 3 drifted tests in `scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`, execute a full `claims:exec` verification pass across all 47 Lean proofs and 133 data tests, and apply the 7 MCP fixes from issue #56 (raises `execution-validation`, 10% weight, and `scientific-impact`, 25% weight).
missing_evidence: The files and experimental results for the 'four-arm agent comparison harness (single agent / isolated workers / centralized swarm / decentralized swarm... Two experiments run, 20 claims each)' claimed in issue #41, which are absent from `captured/tree.txt` and the evidence pack.
A full `scripts/exec/runs/latest.json` run covering all 47 Lean proofs and 133 data tests (the captured `latest.json` only ran 6 data claims: 3 reproduced, 3 drifted).

Sample signed/unsigned `.trig` nanopub files and individual `test-data/claim-tests/<project>/<id>/result.json` + `analysis.py` files to directly inspect code and proof quality rather than relying on `SUMMARY.md` and `lean-reports.txt` counts.
Contents of `claim-sources/cell-geometry/README.md` and its segmenter-bias report (referenced in `repo/README.md` and `captured/forum-feed.json`, but not copied into `repo/`).
summary: Delphisci is an extraordinarily productive and technically rigorous epistemic engine that extracted 1,702 biological and mathematical claims, formalized 47 in Lean 4 without `sorry`, tested 133 against empirical and computational data (including a self-correcting negative control that caught Cellpose-SAM segmenter bias), and deployed live nanopublications and a verified MCP server in under 24 hours. However, judged strictly against the Science Claw rubric, its multi-agent workflow is centrally orchestrated by a human planner rather than a decentralized collective (4/10), and it lacks a committed experimental comparison showing that collective agency outperforms a single agent (3/10, 25% weight).

highest_value_improvement.title: Run and commit a 30-claim 4-arm ablation benchmark (single agent vs. isolated multi-agent vs. routed collective vs. forum-coordinated collective) with autonomous forum handoff
highest_value_improvement.what: Extend `plugins/fittest/route.py` and add a reproducible benchmark runner (`test-data/collective-benchmark/run.py`) over a stratified sample of 30 claims from the 99 decisive data tests in `test-data/claim-tests/` (10 Darwin, 10 Thompson, 10 Wolfram/Levin), plus commit the 20-claim 4-arm harness outputs referenced in issue #41 if they exist outside the repo. Evaluate four arms on the exact same 30 claims: (Arm 1: Single Agent) standalone truth/verdict prediction and single-shot test script by one model (GPT-5.6 Sol alone and Grok 4.7 alone); (Arm 2: Isolated Multi-Agent) unrouted mean of GPT-5.6 Sol + Grok 4.7 truth scores and unverified dataset URLs; (Arm 3: Routed Collective) Fittest disagreement + confidence router (`route.py`) triggering data-test execution on flagged claims; and (Arm 4: Decentralized Forum Loop) 30 claims posted as open tasks to `https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev`, autonomously claimed via `node forum/client.mjs offer` by two non-builder agents (e.g., GPT and Grok workers polling `/api/v1/requests` without human chat intervention), tested, and audited by a blind A9 faithfulness agent (issue #40) that logs `delphi_log_test_result` and catches operationalization/segmenter defects. Amit and Kris can run the `route.py` baseline + 30-claim comparison in parallel while an autonomous cron/loop runs the forum claim-and-audit cycle.
highest_value_improvement.why_this_one: In `rubric.json`, `collective-capability` (25% weight) and `decentralized-agency` (20% weight) together account for 45% of the entire 100-point score, yet they are the project's two lowest scores (3/10 and 4/10, losing 29.5 weighted points). By contrast, `problem-significance` (8/10), `scientific-impact` (7/10), and `execution-validation` (8/10) are already strong and have diminishing returns. `collective-capability` is at 3/10 specifically because `comparison_found.found` is `false`: moving from no comparison to anchor 10 ('a measured comparison in the snapshot (same task, collective vs single agent or isolated agents) showing a clear gain') unlocks a +6 jump on a 0.25-weight criterion (+15.0 weighted points). Simultaneously, running Arm 4 through autonomous polling and claiming on the already-deployed Science Claw forum (`forum/client.mjs` + `delphi_log_test_result`) replaces scripted human batching (`forum/posts/thompson-ch07-04-arc.json`) with genuine shared-state coordination, moving `decentralized-agency` from below anchor 5 (4/10) to 7/10 (+6.0 weighted points) and adding verified A9 faithfulness checks that raise `execution-validation` by +1 (+1.0 weighted point), for a total gain of +22.0 points in ~3-4 hours (~5.5-7.3 points/hour).
highest_value_improvement.effort: 3 to 4 team-hours before Sun Nov 1 13:00 (1.5 hours to extend `plugins/fittest/route.py` with single-model arms and commit the 4-arm comparison table over existing data tests; 2 hours to run an autonomous polling loop where GPT/Grok agents claim open requests on `science-claw-forum.fly.dev`, run A9 faithfulness checks on 10-30 claims, and write results back via MCP).
highest_value_improvement.evidence_that_would_prove_it: `test-data/collective-benchmark/results.json` and `test-data/collective-benchmark/SUMMARY.md` containing the 4-arm comparison table (Arm x N=30 claims x accuracy vs. ground-truth verdicts x silent-failure rate x valid-URL rate x token cost), updated `plugins/fittest/routing-results.json` showing single-model (GPT-5.6 Sol alone, Grok 4.7 alone) vs. collective accuracy, and `captured/forum-feed.json` / `captured/forum-requests.json` showing non-`delphisci` agent accounts autonomously claiming requests (`status: done`), posting `delphi:test-result` payloads, and writing `test-data/claim-tests/<project>/<id>/faithfulness.json` files.
